name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
about: A coastal links course on California’s Monterey Peninsula, with small greens and fairways along Stillwater Cove.

rankings.label: No. 1 public course in America
rankings.publisher: Golf Digest, as reported by Pebble Beach

name: Torrey Pines South Course
about: A municipal course above the Pacific Ocean in La Jolla, California.

events.title: U.S. Open
events.text: The South Course hosted both editions; this history does not apply to the North Course.

name: Pinehurst No. 2
about: Pinehurst’s celebrated No. 2 course in the North Carolina Sandhills.

events.title: U.S. Open
events.text: The championship returned to No. 2 for the fourth time.

rankings.label: No. 2 · Top 100 Courses You Can Play in the U.S.
rankings.publisher: GOLF, as reported by Pinehurst Resort

name: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort
about: The original Bandon Dunes course on Oregon’s coast, designed by David McLay Kidd and opened in 1999.

events.title: U.S. Amateur
events.text: Bandon Dunes hosted championship play; Bandon Trails was the stroke-play co-host.

name: Tpc Sawgrass Dyes Valley Course
about: Dye’s Valley opened in 1987. It is a separate layout from the adjacent PLAYERS Stadium Course.

events.title: Web.com Tour Championship
events.text: TPC identifies Dye’s Valley as a host of the Web.com Tour Championship.

name: Whistling Straits
about: A Wisconsin golf destination on Lake Michigan. Its Straits and Irish layouts are separate courses.

events.title: Ryder Cup · Straits Course
events.text: The Straits Course hosted the 43rd Ryder Cup. This event belongs to the Straits layout, not the Irish.
